# The flows that rivus finds in its own code as it is on macOS (TestDogfood, the darwin view: GOOS=darwin, read statically on any system). Same
# format and rules as dogfood-flows.txt (the Linux view); this view also reads the code that is only for macOS: the sandbox (internal/sandbox) and the
# call of it that runs the programs of a Rust project (cmd/rivus/isolate_sandbox_darwin.go). What the flags name (the project, the
# extractor, a path to read) reaches the programs that the sandbox runs and the files it prepares: that is what a CLI that runs a
# build under a sandbox does, and it is what the analysis must find in its own code.

cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).analyze [os.Create]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).analyze [os.Create]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).analyze [os.Create]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).extractInto [os/exec.Command]  # the extractor command of -extractor (or -lang) is run: the same flow as extractRaw before the function was renamed
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.common).loadRules [os.Open]  # the rule files that the flags name (-rules, -rules-dir) are opened to be read: what the flags say reaches the file that rivus reads
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.common).projectRuleFiles [os.ReadDir]  # the directory of -C is listed to find the rule files of the project: the path of the project is what the flag says
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.isolationOpts).extractRustSandboxedTo [os.MkdirAll]  # the directories of the isolation of the Rust extractor are made under the paths that the flags name (-isolation-*, -C): ADR-093, the same group as isolate.go
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> (*cmd/rivus.isolationOpts).extractRustSandboxedTo [os.ReadFile]  # the files of the project (-C) that the isolation reads to decide what to give the sandbox: ADR-093, the same group as isolate.go
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.cargoLockVersions [os.ReadFile]  # Cargo.lock in the directory of -C is read for the versions of the crates (summary.unverified_versions)
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.cargoVolume [os.ReadFile]  # the Cargo.lock and the configuration of the project (-C) are read to decide the volumes of the sandbox: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.cargoVolume [os.ReadFile]  # the Cargo.lock and the configuration of the project (-C) are read to decide the volumes of the sandbox: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.dartLockVersions [os.ReadFile]  # pubspec.lock in the directory of -C is read for the versions of the packages (summary.unverified_versions)
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.dropConfigOfCargoHome [os.RemoveAll]  # the configuration that the project (-C, -isolation-read) put in the Cargo home of the run is removed before the sandbox starts: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.planFetch [os.ReadFile]  # Cargo.lock of the project (-C) is read to plan the fetch of the crates: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.projectToolchain [os.ReadFile]  # the toolchain file of the project (-C) is read to choose the toolchain of the run: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.projectToolchain [os.ReadFile]  # the toolchain file of the project (-C) is read to choose the toolchain of the run: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.readIR [os.Open]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> cmd/rivus.readIRSpill [os.Open]  # the file that holds the IR beside the run is opened to be read back (the spill of ADR-123; the path comes from the flags of the run): the same flow as readIR
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/frontend/gossa.countTestFiles [os.ReadDir]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/graphdb.hashFile [os.Open]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/sandbox.Run [os/exec.Command]  # the project, the extractor and the paths that the flags name are what the sandbox runs and prepares (the run of a build under the sandbox: docs/DESIGN-macos-sandbox.md)
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/vcs.findGitDir [os.ReadFile]  # the .git file of the project (-C) is read to find the Git directory (a worktree has a file there): the path of the project is what the flag says
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/vcs.readHead [os.ReadFile]  # HEAD, the refs and packed-refs of the Git directory of the project (-C) are read for the commit of the report: the path of the project is what the flag says
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/vcs.readHead [os.ReadFile]  # HEAD, the refs and packed-refs of the Git directory of the project (-C) are read for the commit of the report: the path of the project is what the flag says
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/vcs.readHead [os.ReadFile]  # HEAD, the refs and packed-refs of the Git directory of the project (-C) are read for the commit of the report: the path of the project is what the flag says
cmd/rivus.runAnalyze -> internal/vcs.readHead [os.ReadFile]  # HEAD, the refs and packed-refs of the Git directory of the project (-C) are read for the commit of the report: the path of the project is what the flag says

cmd/rivus.runResolve -> (*cmd/rivus.isolationOpts).extractRustSandboxedTo [os.ReadFile]  # the files of the project (-C) that the isolation reads to decide what to give the sandbox: ADR-093, the same group as isolate.go
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.cargoLockVersions [os.ReadFile]  # Cargo.lock in the directory of -C is read for the versions of the crates (summary.unverified_versions)
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.cargoVolume [os.ReadFile]  # the Cargo.lock and the configuration of the project (-C) are read to decide the volumes of the sandbox: ADR-093

cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.dartLockVersions [os.ReadFile]  # pubspec.lock in the directory of -C is read for the versions of the packages (summary.unverified_versions)
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.dropConfigOfCargoHome [os.RemoveAll]  # the configuration that the project (-C, -isolation-read) put in the Cargo home of the run is removed before the sandbox starts: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.planFetch [os.ReadFile]  # Cargo.lock of the project (-C) is read to plan the fetch of the crates: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.projectToolchain [os.ReadFile]  # the toolchain file of the project (-C) is read to choose the toolchain of the run: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.projectToolchain [os.ReadFile]  # the toolchain file of the project (-C) is read to choose the toolchain of the run: ADR-093
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.readIR [os.Open]  # the same kind of flow as in the Linux view: what a flag names reaches a file or a program of the command that uses it
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> cmd/rivus.readIRSpill [os.Open]  # the file that holds the IR beside the run is opened to be read back (the spill of ADR-123; the path comes from the flags of the run): the same flow as readIR

cmd/rivus.runResolve -> internal/sandbox.Run [os/exec.Command]  # the project, the extractor and the paths that the flags name are what the sandbox runs and prepares (the run of a build under the sandbox: docs/DESIGN-macos-sandbox.md)
cmd/rivus.runResolve -> internal/vcs.findGitDir [os.ReadFile]  # the .git file of the project (-C) is read to find the Git directory (a worktree has a file there): the path of the project is what the flag says

cmd/rivus.runSites -> (*cmd/rivus.analyzeOpts).extractInto [os/exec.Command]  # the extractor command of -extractor (or -lang) is run: the same flow as extractRaw before the function was renamed
